assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a genuinely new observational window: a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector that saw a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, later tied to the blazar TXS 0506+056 and to the Galactic plane. This is exactly the combination of detector invention and discovery that I find most compelling, and the physics (cosmic-ray origin, neutrino astronomy) will last.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the only credited name and is widely seen as the originator and driving force of IceCube. The supplied credit supports a one-person configuration, but a collaboration of this size makes the decisive individual contributions hard to separate (e.g. the roles of the AMANDA predecessor and other leaders); I cannot independently verify the internal history.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been seen by IceCube since 2013 and corroborated in several channels and by ANTARES/Baikal-GVD hints; the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 results are strong but statistically more modest, and the Galactic-plane result is recent. Recognition looks timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Sources of the diffuse flux are only partly identified, and independent confirmation by a second large telescope is still limited.
A single-person award for a large collaboration could be contested; other leaders might need to be considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measurement of the last unknown mixing angle theta-13 with reactor antineutrinos was a precision, clean and decisive result that unlocked the search for leptonic CP violation and the mass ordering. Clear and original, with a straightforward experimental message and robust systematics control.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) announced nearly simultaneously in 2012; Double Chooz and T2K also contributed, so credit is shared across several experiments. The supplied triplet is a plausible configuration but leaves out Double Chooz leaders, and the role of the earlier proposals is uncertain to me.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several reactor and accelerator experiments, values stable and now precisely measured. Fully mature.
uncertainties: Priority among Daya Bay, RENO and Double Chooz is sensitive; excluding one group is a judgment call.
The 2015 prize already honoured neutrino oscillations, so the committee may regard this as a follow-on rather than a fresh discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping) delivered a step change in frequency metrology, with fractional uncertainty at the 1e-18 level and applications in geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a future redefinition of the second. An instrument-led advance with a clear idea and demonstrated lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and Ye led the demonstration of the most precise realizations. A two-laureate prize is natural, but the contributions of ion-clock groups and of the comb and laser-stabilization work already honoured in 2005 complicate the picture; I am relying on the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reached comparable accuracy and clock comparisons agree, so the confirmation is strong. The redefinition of the second is still pending, though that is not a prerequisite.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes (frequency combs, ion control) may reduce appetite.
Outside my own expertise in atomic physics; I would defer to colleagues on the relative priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS detectors made the 2012 Higgs discovery possible, and I appreciate the decades of detector R&D, calibration and systematics work behind it. The impact on particle physics is huge and durable, but the discovery itself was recognised in 2013.
assessment.attribution: The three named people were the founding spokespersons and conceptual leaders, but thousands of physicists built the detectors. Awards for instrumentation of large collaborations are rare and the allocation of credit to three people is contentious; the exact boundaries are unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Entirely mature; the detectors have operated for over a decade and the results are independently cross-confirmed between the two experiments.
uncertainties: Committee tradition favours the discovery or the theory rather than the apparatus, and 2013 already addressed the Higgs.
Individual credit is spread across large collaborations and could not be settled by the supplied names alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the cosmic microwave background into a precision tool, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the Universe and establishing the concordance LCDM model. A superb space instrument whose results are still the backbone of cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument and calibration figure, and Spergel was central to the analysis and cosmological interpretation. The proposed trio is plausible, but the mission credit also involves Wilkinson, Wollack, Hinshaw and others, so allocation is not fully clear.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and surpassed by Planck and ground experiments; very mature, though the question is whether it is still timely since COBE (2006) and the 2019 cosmology prize already covered the field.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the COBE prize and the 2019 award reduces novelty.
Whether the committee sees WMAP as a new discovery or as a refinement is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry underpins inertial sensing, gravimetry, tests of the equivalence principle and measurement of fundamental constants. As a measurement technology it opens new precision regimes, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard demonstrated early atom interferometers and Bordé developed the theoretical framework with Ramsey-Bordé fringes; Kasevich made the atomic-fountain gyroscope and gradiometer breakthroughs. Other groups (Chu, Rasel, Mlynek, Keith) were also decisive, so the three-person split is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used in commercial and fundamental physics, though the most ambitious applications (gravitational-wave detection, dark-matter searches) are still developing.
uncertainties: Chu's 1997 prize and others already covered related atom cooling and trapping techniques.
The priority conflict among interferometer pioneers is not resolved in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theory-prediction-then-experiment story: the magic-angle flat bands and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the whole field of moire materials. Condensed matter lies outside my own expertise, and I would rely on colleagues, but the originality and breadth of impact are evident.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative prediction in 2011 and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery, which is a clean theory-plus-experiment pairing. Other contributors (e.g. Cao, Santos, Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) complicate the claims.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still under active debate, so the interpretation is not yet fully settled.
uncertainties: Open questions on the pairing mechanism and sample-to-sample variation.
Credit for early theoretical work on twisted bilayers may need broader consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond created a robust solid-state qubit and room-temperature nanoscale sensor. As a sensor technology with a wide user base, it appeals to my instrument-oriented view, though quantum information is not my field.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-NV optical detection and spin control in 1997 and following years; Lukin contributed much of the quantum-sensing and quantum-register development. Other leaders (Awschalom, Hanson, Budker, Hollenberg) are also strong claimants, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and commercialised, with strong independent confirmation; applications in biology and materials are still evolving.
uncertainties: Overlap with other solid-state spin-qubit candidates and unresolved credit among several groups.
I would defer to the colleagues with expertise in quantum optics and condensed matter on relative merit.
